newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN GO TOP AFTER 2-0 WIN AT KARLSRUHE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN GO TOP AFTER 2-0 WIN AT KARLSRUHE.

text.p: Bayern Munich ended a turbulent week off the pitch with a 2-0 victory at Karlsruhe on Sunday to take over top spot in the German first division.
Two goals from striker Alexander Zickler in the 30th and 90th minutes helped the Bavarians take a two-point lead after a week in which striker Juergen Klinsmann said he was leaving the club.

Bayern have 49 points from 24 games. VfB Stuttgart, who won 4-0 at struggling Fortuna Duesseldorf on Friday, and Bayer Leverkusen, 2-1 winners at bottom club Freiburg on Saturday, are level on 47 points in second and third places respectively.

Last week's leaders Borussia Dortmund have slipped to fourth a further point behind after losing 3-1 to Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. It was the reigning champions' first defeat at home for more than a year.

Klinsmann, who said he would be quitting at the end of the season because he did not fit in at Bayern, was unable to play in Sunday evening's game because of suspension and has been allowed to take a five-day holiday.

Bayern's first goal was slightly controversial since Zickler's marker Dirk Schuster fell to the ground as the two players ran together without the ball towards the right-hand side of the box during a Bayern attack.
But experienced referee Hellmut Krug did not give a foul. Zickler was completely unmarked when he received a pass in the area and lobbed the ball cleverly past the left-hand post.

Zickler's second goal came after a counter-attack when Karlsruhe goalkeeper Claus Reitmaier had run down the pitch into the Bayern penalty area to try and help the home side equalise in the dying seconds.
Zickler raced to the other end and put the ball into an empty net.
